To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multiscale molecular dynamics simulation can be used to define the mechanism of interaction of PTEN and Ci-VSP PTN domains with PIP containing membranes.

the interaction of the phosphatidylinostol phosphate phosphatase PTEN with membranes is characterized by a two step process in which the protein first interacts with the membrane electrostatically and then undergoes a conformational change that brings its active site into close proximity with PIP3.

(1) PTEN and Ci-VSP interact with PIP-containing membranes through a mechanism in which an initial encounter of the protein with the bilayer is followed, in both cases, by reorientation of PTEN and Ci VSP to optimize their interactions with the PIP molecules in membranes; and (2) in both proteins, PIP3 molecules bind to the active site in a manner that may be catalytically non-productive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the interactions of PTEN and Ci-VSP proteins with phosphatidylinositide-containing membranes.
understanding how the PTEN and Ci-VSP PDs bind PIPs in membranes.
the interaction of the PD and C2 domains of PTEN and Ci-VSP with PIP-containing membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both proteins interact with PIP-containing bilayers in an electrostatics-driven manner, but that the nature and details of this interaction are different.
PTEN and Ci-VSP interact with PIP-containing bilayers via a common mechanism of initial electrostatic encounter, but with a subsequent reorientation for PTEN and direct binding for Ci-VSP.
the PTEN and Ci-VSP proteins interact with PIP-containing membranes in a similar manner but that the PTEN domain alone does not bind to PIP-containing bilayers in a catalyticaly productive manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C2 domain of PTEN is a membrane binding module and that it interacts with PIPs through a novel two-step process, whereas the C2 domain in Ci-VSP is a membrane insertion module.

PTEN and Ci-VSP interact with membranes via electrostatic interactions with the phosphate groups of PIP molecules, and the binding of the PIP3 molecule close to the active sites of both proteins is a key step for their function as lipid phosphatases.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the PTEN and Ci-VSP PTENS are able to interact with PIP-containing bilayers, but that a subsequent conformational change may be required for productive catalysis to occur.
the PTEN domain can interact with PIP-containing membranes via a novel mechanism involving an initial electrostatically-driven encounter followed by a reorientation step.

the PTEN domains from both proteins bind to PIP-containing lipid membranes through a mechanism that is distinct from that of other PIP phosphatases, and that this interaction is likely to be a key determinant of the function of these proteins in cells.
